audit.whatIsWrong: The whole full layer tracks an ability called 'Yasuo Path Maker'. Path Maker is K'SANTE's own W. Yasuo has no such ability — his kit is Way of the Wanderer, Steel Tempest, Wind Wall, Sweeping Blade, Last Breath. The tracked-cooldown line, the loading screen, the focus tag, the TL;DR and eight report/breakdown fields all name the player's own ability as the enemy's.
audit.why: champ-data/_kits/yasuo.json lists W as Wind Wall, 25/23/21/19/17s, 'Creates a moving wall that blocks all enemy projectiles for 4 seconds'. That is the cooldown worth tracking, because K'Sante's Q carries the projectile flag and Wind Wall deletes it outright.
audit.corrected: Every 'Path Maker' reference on the Yasuo page is now Wind Wall, with its 25s rank-1 cooldown and 4-second duration stated.

audit.whatIsWrong: Levels 4-5 were Skill despite the why calling it 'your tank lane-control peak', and both late rows were K'Sante despite the why saying 'He out-scales hard'.
audit.why: Packet chart reads Skill / K'Sante / K'Sante / K'Sante / Skill / Skill / Yasuo, matching the whys and the 50.72% win rate over 1459 games.
audit.corrected: Rows 3, 5 and 6 flipped in matched full/content pairs.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spikes never gave a cooldown and never mentioned Yasuo's passive shield.
audit.why: Wind Wall 25s at rank 1 down to 17s maxed, 4 seconds of blocking; Steel Tempest 4s with the 2-stack whirlwind knockup that is the only setup for Last Breath (70/50/30s); Way of the Wanderer builds a shield whenever he moves, which absorbs the opener of your burst.
audit.corrected: Spikes now carry Wind Wall's numbers, the 2-stack Steel Tempest knockup as the R condition, and the passive shield as the thing to pop first.

audit.whatIsWrong: early, mid and late were written in the first person, and the 2-stack Ntofo shockwave was called a knock-up.
audit.why: Site voice is second person, and Riot's Q text says the shockwave pulls enemies in — the knock-back and stun are Path Maker.
audit.corrected: Rewritten in second person with the pull named correctly. The packet's suspectName 'My All Out' is a false positive — it is the first-person phrasing, not a fabricated ability; All Out is the real R name.

edits.before: Level 1 is even — I only have Q so I just farm and don't walk into his Steel Tempest pokes while he stacks his tornado. The real shift is level 3: once Path Maker and the full Ntofo Strikes are online, I can W a Yasuo who steps up to last-hit and Q3 him into a knockup before his crit pattern means anything. Note his Windwall does nothing if I engage in melee — it only eats my Q if I throw it from range, so close the gap first, then poke. Don't burn W early; bait his E-dash and punish him when it's down.
edits.after: Level 1 is even — you only have Q, so farm and stay out of his Steel Tempest pokes while he stacks the tornado. The shift is level 3: with Path Maker and Ntofo Strikes online you can W a Yasuo who steps up to last-hit and pull him in before his crit pattern means anything. Wind Wall does nothing if you engage in melee — it only eats a Q thrown from range, so close first, then poke. Don't burn W early: bait the dash, and note his passive shield builds while he walks, so pop it before you commit.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are mine as a tank — I trade around his E cooldown, soak his crit autos with my bulk, and bank small leads because he can't kite a champ who walks him down with passive move speed. At 6, All Out is a trap if I misuse it: the duelist conversion wins me a straight 1v1, but it strips my armor exactly when his Steel Tempest knockup and E let him answer back, so only commit R when both are down. Bait the Windwall by faking a Q, then engage in melee where it's worthless.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are yours as a tank — you trade around Sweeping Blade, soak his crit autos with your bulk, and bank small leads because he cannot kite a champion who walks him down. At 6 All Out is a trap if misused: the duelist conversion wins a straight 1v1 but strips your armour exactly when a 2-stack Steel Tempest knockup hands him free Last Breath, so commit R only once that is spent. Fake a Q to bait Wind Wall — 25s at rank 1 — then fight in melee where it is worthless.

edits.before: This is where it slips. Yasuo is a hard scaler — once he hits crit items and his power spikes, Windwall blanks every ranged poke I have and my whole tank identity falls apart against a champ whose crit DPS doesn't care about armor stacking. My All Out gives me damage but takes my bulk, and a full-build Yasuo just out-DPSes that stripped profile. So I have to cash my mid-game leads before two items: end the game, or pivot to peeling him off my carries with R's knockback rather than trying to solo-duel him.
